identity.real_world_identity_notes: The PMR telemetry name S7R resolves to the Saleen S7-R, specifically the 2004 car named by PMR. The exact 2004 evidence describes the later sequential S7-R/EVO configuration. This is kept separate from the existing saleen-s7-r-gt1 record, whose identity is explicitly the distinct 2005 second-series GT1 representation. Early 2001 H-pattern/clutch instructions and later 2010 Xtrac data are retained as family or adjacent-variant evidence, not silently promoted to every 2004 car.

Project Motor Racing's official vehicle page explicitly calls the car the 2004 Saleen S7-R and places it in GT. A separate exact-scope account identifies a 2004 S7-R EVO, chassis 029R, and states that its gearbox is sequential with six speeds. The existing curated record is explicitly labelled a 2005 GT1 representation, so a new year-bounded proposal avoids silently collapsing the 2004 and 2005 specifications.

The exact 2004 S7-R EVO account states six speeds; the later technical listing independently describes the S7-R family as six-speed. The exact 2004 source calls the gearbox sequential with six speeds. The later technical source and Johnny Mowlem's revision history corroborate that the later S7-R family used sequential gearboxes. The exact 2004 source explicitly calls the gearbox sequential, and the driver interview separates the later sequential version from the early H-pattern version.
